title: Gabber's root condition implies lifting of sections of etale algebras
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that (a) $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and (b) every monic polynomial $f(T)=T^n(T-1)+a_nT^n+\dots+a_1T+a_0\in A[T]$ with $n\ge1$ and $a_0,\dots,a_n\in I$ has a root $\alpha\in1+I$. Then for every ring map $A\to A'$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every $A$-algebra map $\sigma:A'\to A/I$ there is an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A'\to A$ whose composite with the quotient map $A\to A/I$ is $\sigma$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), implication (5)$\Rightarrow$(2) and its proof (paragraphs from 'Assume (5). We will show that (2) holds' to the end of the proof): the section gives $A'/IA'\cong A/I\times C$ (Algebra Lemmas 00U7 lemma-map-between-etale and 00U8 lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented); integral closure $B'$ of $A$ in $A'$ and Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type, line 2502); a finite subalgebra $B''$ and Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290) give $f$ as in (b) with $f(b)=0$; the root $a\in1+I$ splits $A[T]/(f)$ and hence $B'$ and $A'$; Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski, line 2265) concludes

proof.text: Apply the integral idempotent section-factor construction to obtain e, an integral map A->B[1/e], a bijective quotient map, and a compatible rho extending sigma.
The localization B[1/e] is etale over A, hence flat and finitely presented. Apply the Zariski-pair flat integral isomorphism theorem to its structure map, obtaining bijectivity.

Promote the bijective structure map to an A-algebra equivalence Phi. Compose the localization map B->B[1/e] with Phi inverse to define tau. On an element x, rho(Phi(Phi inverse(x/1)))=rho(x/1)=sigma(x); rho commutes with A, so this is precisely the desired quotient identity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09XI (5) implies (2): construction split at the integral first factor; final Tag 0ELZ isomorphism and inversion formalized explicitly.
